title: The rational Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties

result.label: Rational Hodge for CM abelian varieties, with stated consequences
result.statement: Let A be a complex CM abelian variety. For every integer p≥0, the Betti cycle-class map cl_B: CH^p(A)_Q → H^(2p)(A,Q) ∩ H^(p,p)(A) is surjective. The family also states the generalized Hodge conjecture for CM abelian varieties, the Tate conjecture for abelian varieties over finite fields, and the Hodge standard conjecture for abelian varieties in arbitrary characteristic.
result.detail: The main spine constructs algebraic representatives for four-factor tensors, assembles them into arbitrary balanced CM tensors, and then derives the three stated consequences. The companion manuscripts are related work, not premises in this spine.
result.roleNote: Theorem 1.1 is the direct result. Corollaries 8.2–8.4 are consequences derived from it through Milne’s theorems and the generalized-Hodge correspondence argument; they are not alternative proofs of the main theorem.

nodes.label: André/Deligne reduction
nodes.detail: The introduction cites Deligne and André for the reduction of a CM Hodge class to a sum of pullbacks of split Weil classes. That reduction identifies classes whose algebraicity would suffice; it does not construct the cycles. This node is orientation only and has no edge into the paper’s spine.

nodes.label: Hazama four-label relations
nodes.detail: Hazama’s arrangement method spans its rational balance kernel by antipodal pairs and four-label square relations. The introduction cites this as motivation; §2.3 proves the tensor reduction used here. This node has no edge into the selected spine.

nodes.label: Scalar descent
nodes.detail: If a rational vector t has every Galois conjugate in a complex-linear subspace P, then t lies in (T∩P)⊗Q Q. The same assertion applies to maps of a fixed Hodge type in a Hom space.

nodes.label: Degree-one realization
nodes.detail: Pullback identifies Hom(A,B)⊗Q with rational Hodge maps from H^1(B,Q) to H^1(A,Q). A rational Hodge map from a smooth projective surface S to B is an integer multiple of a morphism S→B after composing with the Albanese map.

nodes.label: Surface criterion
nodes.detail: Four rational Hodge maps h_i: U(v_i)→H^1(S,Q) and vectors α_i on the prescribed embedding lines with nonzero cup-product integral force the four-factor Künneth line to be algebraic. Four divisor kernels convert the surface functional into a vector on that exact line.

nodes.label: Nonzero mixed theta period
nodes.fullLabel: §4 · Theta differentials and a nonzero mixed period
nodes.detail: Constructs a nonzero mixed period with two holomorphic and two antiholomorphic factors on a compact arithmetic quotient of the complex two-ball. The finite theta input and quotient stay fixed while compact-place data vary, and the rank-two theta tensor packages the wedges.

nodes.label: CM extraction
nodes.detail: Degree-one CM extraction and finite-family CM extraction identify theta one-form classes with spans of rational Hodge maps from the selected CM lines. Algebraic Hecke operators, a Frobenius polynomial, ordinary isogeny neighbors, and scalar descent supply the arithmetic identification.

nodes.label: Four-factor construction
nodes.detail: Places the finitely many theta families on one projective surface, expands the nonzero period over the finite family, and applies the surface criterion. This produces the algebraic four-factor line for each required quadruple.

nodes.label: Four-factor switch
nodes.detail: Let E be a Galois CM field and let odd sign functions v_1,…,v_4 satisfy v_1+v_2=v_3+v_4. Under the Künneth inclusion, the line U(v_1)_1 ⊗ U(v_2)_1 ⊗ U(v_3)_c ⊗ U(v_4)_c is algebraic. Section 7 proves this via the surface construction.

nodes.label: Assembly from four factors
nodes.detail: If the four-factor switch holds for every Galois CM field and every balanced quadruple, then every rational Hodge class on every complex CM abelian variety is algebraic. Two-row switches connect lists with the same type sum; algebraic polarization pairings contract intermediate factors; scalar descent returns the coefficient field to Q.

nodes.label: Rational Hodge for CM varieties
nodes.fullLabel: Theorem 1.1 · Rational Hodge for CM abelian varieties
nodes.detail: For every complex CM abelian variety A and every p≥0, the Betti cycle-class map from rational Chow classes to rational Hodge classes of type (p,p) is surjective.

nodes.label: Generalized Hodge
nodes.detail: For a rational Hodge substructure W of H^k(A,Q) with W(r) effective, there is a closed algebraic subset Z of codimension at least r whose complement has W in the kernel of the restriction map.

nodes.label: Tate conjecture
nodes.detail: For every abelian variety over a finite field, every codimension, and every prime different from the characteristic, the cycle-class map from rational Chow classes to Galois-invariant ℓ-adic classes is surjective; numerical and homological equivalence coincide.

nodes.label: Hodge standard conjecture
nodes.detail: For an abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, numerical and ℓ-adic homological equivalence coincide on rational algebraic cycles, and the intersection form on primitive classes is positive definite after extension to R.
